gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The exam, the results of ___ will be published on Friday, was very difficult.
gaps.hint: quantity noun + of + thing in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'The results of which' joins the clauses formally; 'of whom' is for people and 'of them' cannot link clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The bridge, on ___ repairs are still continuing, will reopen in May.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern; 'where' cannot follow a preposition, and 'that' is barred from non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: It was Marie Curie ___ discoveries changed modern medicine.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose discoveries' means 'Marie Curie's discoveries'; 'who's' would mean 'who is'.

gaps.sentence: He showed me the drawer in ___ the keys were kept.
gaps.explanation: 'In which' is the formal relative pattern for things; 'in where' is ungrammatical.

gaps.hint: after 'all', the relative pronoun is not 'what'
gaps.explanation: 'All that glitters' is the proverb pattern; 'what' cannot follow 'all', and 'which' is avoided after 'all'.

gaps.sentence: The book ___ I borrowed from the library is two weeks overdue.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things; 'who' refers only to people and 'where' to places.
